items.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I used to play that. I like that. Punch Miller still plays that down in New Orleans. Yes. You might have heard him.

ctx.x: I don't remember that song about if you're broken hearted and your man is out of town, go to the river and jump right up. Take your chance. Take your chance. Take your chance. Make Mennowiller. If he don't come back, let me tell you what to do. Jump right up with boys, cause you ain't no more than you. Cause I thought my man would kiss him morning, noon, and night. I'd wipe you clothes and keep you clean, try to treat him right. Then he went and left me after all I tried to do. The way he treated you, he'd do the…

I used to play that. I like that. Punch Miller still plays that down in New Orleans. Yes. You might have heard him. He was a solid screen for a long time. Yes. I was born. I ain't been far. Yeah. What about your, uh, back to your family. Now you say your mother was a dancer.
Yes, she was the best. And frankly, God, anybody that doesn't know. And your father?
